messages:
sana: Observed read-after-write in staging after an eviction ran right after a lease revoke. Short timeline below.

eric: Paste logs?

sana: snippet:
```
[2026-03-19T09:12:30Z] lease_revoke epoch=87 prefix=prfx/A42
[2026-03-19T09:12:30Z] evict_decide epoch=86 prefix=prfx/A42 node=node-3
[2026-03-19T09:12:30Z] client_cursor read -> tombstone
```

sana: Root cause hypothesis: eviction apply can proceed with a stale epoch if fanout of lease_revoke hasn't reached the evict worker. We stash observed_epoch at schedule time but currently don't always re-read before apply to keep fastpath.

zoe: Sigh. Two obvious mitigations: 1) always re-read meta at apply (safe, more RTTs), 2) add a revoke fence/marker that workers honor (less sync but new meta).

ben: Hybrid idea: keep fastpath but do a cheap meta check at apply from local meta-cache; if epoch mismatch or cache miss, backoff and retry a few times. Add a high-priority fence enqueue on revoke so common case wins.

e ric: (typo) I mean eric: That seems reasonable. But must handle cross-node reordering and splits: if split occurs, epoch semantics should map to new ranges. Add split/merge rules in RFC.

zoe: Metrics: evict_epoch_skip, evict_after_revoke. Alert if after_revoke ratio > 0.1%. Add chaos test that delays fanout to validate.

sana: Rollout plan: implement fence + apply-time epoch-check + local cache invalidation on fanout. Unit + chaos tests, canary flag=evict_epoch_check at 25% region.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary started region=eu-west-1 flag=evict_epoch_check=true pct=25

ben: I'll draft RFC covering tradeoffs, perf impact, and split semantics. Also add a small simulation harness command in repo: `go test ./evictsim -run TestRevokeRace -count=1`.

sana: Thanks all, opening RFC link shortly.
